{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01MBdhRXFR61sBjxatWwccwz","type":"tool_result","content":"=== persistence/__init__.py\n\"\"\"Persistence for this Target. Shipped engines plus the schema generated from DATABASE.md.\"\"\"\n\nfrom .db import Database, PersistenceError, UnknownOperation\nfrom .schema import SCHEMA, open_database\n\n__all__ = [\"Database\", \"PersistenceError\", \"SCHEMA\", \"UnknownOperation\", \"open_database\"]\n=== persistence/db.py\n\"\"\"Persistence access for a Drydock Target.\n\nThis file is shipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. Do not edit it here: edit\n``DATABASE.md`` and rebuild. It is hardened and tested once, in Drydock's own suite, so every\nTarget inherits a persistence layer that has already passed rather than one re-derived from prose\non each build.\n\nThe application-facing surface is ``Database``. One attribute per declared table, one method per\ndeclared access pattern::\n\n    db = Database(dsn, SCHEMA)\n    ticket = db.tickets.get(id=7)\n    open_tickets = db.tickets.list(status=\"open\")\n\n``schema.py`` beside this file is generated from ``DATABASE.md`` and carries the tables, the\noperations, and the row types.  gone = book_service.add_book(fresh_db, \"Gone\", \"A\")\n\n    assert book_service.remove_book(fresh_db, gone.id) is True\n\n    assert book_service.list_books(fresh_db) == [keep]\n\n\ndef test_remove_book_returns_false_for_unknown_id(fresh_db: Database) -> None:\n    assert book_service.remove_book(fresh_db, 999999) is False\n\n\ndef test_remove_book_second_removal_returns_false(fresh_db: Database) -> None:\n    book = book_service.add_book(fresh_db, \"Once\", \"A\")\n    book_service.remove_book(fresh_db, book.id)\n\n    assert book_service.remove_book(fresh_db, book.id) is False\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"title, author\",\n    [(\"Dune\", \"Frank Herbert\"), (\"  Dune  \", \"  Frank Herbert  \"), (\"T\", \"A\")],\n)\ndef test_validate_book_input_accepts_non_blank_text(title: str, author: str) -> None:\n    assert book_service.validate_book_input(title, author) is None\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"title, author, field\",\n    [\n        (\"\", \"A\", \"title\"),\n        (\"   \", \"A\", \"title\"),\n        (None, \"A\", \"title\"),\n        (42, \"A\", \"title\"),\n        (\"T\", \"\", \"author\"),\n        (\"T\", \"\\t\\n\", \"author\"),\n        (\"T\", None, \"author\"),\n    ],\n)\ndef test_validate_book_input_names_the_offending_field(title, author, field: str) -> None:\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as error:\n        book_service.validate_book_input(title, author)\n\n    assert field in str(error.value)\n\n\ndef test_validate_book_input_names_both_fields_when_both_are_blank() -> None:\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as error:\n        book_service.validate_book_input(\"\", \"\")\n\n    assert \"title\" in str(error.value)\n    assert \"author\" in book: POST /books answers 201 with the stored book, and the stored row reads back.\"\"\"\n\nfrom flask.testing import FlaskClient\n\nfrom persistence import Database\n\n\ndef test_post_answers_201_with_stored_book_fields(fresh_client: FlaskClient) -> None:\n    response = fresh_client.post(\"/books\", json={\"title\": \"Dune\", \"author\": \"Frank Herbert\"})\n\n    assert response.status_code == 201\n    body = response.get_json()\n    assert isinstance(body[\"id\"], int)\n    assert body[\"title\"] == \"Dune\"\n    assert body[\"author\"] == \"Frank Herbert\"\n\n\ndef test_post_response_body_carries_exactly_id_title_and_author(fresh_client: FlaskClient) -> None:\n    response = fresh_client.post(\"/books\", json={\"title\": \"Dune\", \"author\": \"Frank Herbert\"})\n\n    assert set(response.get_json()) == {\"id\", \"title\", \"author\"}\n\n\ndef test_posted_book_reads_back_from_store(fresh_client: FlaskClient, fresh_db: Database) -> None:\n    body = fresh_client.post(\"/books\", json={\"title\": \"Dune\", \"author\": \"Frank Herbert\"}).get_json()\n\n    row = fresh_db.books.get(id=body[\"id\"])\n\n    assert row is not None\n    assert (row.id, row.title, row.author) == (body[\"id\"], \"Dune\", \"Frank Herbert\")\n\n\ndef test_stored_title_and_author_keep_the_supplied_whitespace(fresh_client: FlaskClient) -> None:\n    response = fresh_client.post(\"/books\", json={\"title\": \"  Dune  \", \"author\": \" Frank Herbert \"})\n\n    body = response.get_json()\n    assert body[\"title\"] == \"  Dune  \"\n    assert body[\"author\"] == \" Frank Herbert \"\n\n\ndef test_two_books_added_in_sequence_receive_ascending_ids(fresh_client: FlaskClient) -> None:\n    first = fresh_client.post(\"/books\", json={\"title\": \"One\", \"author\": \"A\"}).get_json()\n    second = fresh_client.post(\"/books\", json={\"title\": \"Two\", \"author\": \"A\"}).get_json()\n\n    assert first[\"id\"] < response.status_code == 200\n    assert response.get_json() == []\n\n\ndef test_list_returns_titles_in_the_order_they_were_added(fresh_client: FlaskClient) -> None:\n    titles = [\"Ulysses\", \"Dune\", \"Emma\"]\n    for title in titles:\n        _add(fresh_client, title)\n\n    listed = fresh_client.get(\"/books\").get_json()\n\n    assert [book[\"title\"] for book in listed] == titles\n\n\ndef test_list_returns_added_ids_in_submission_order(fresh_client: FlaskClient) -> None:\n    created = [_add(fresh_client, f\"Book {n}\") for n in range(4)]\n\n    listed_ids = [book[\"id\"] for book in fresh_client.get(\"/books\").get_json()]\n\n    assert listed_ids == created\n\n\ndef test_each_listed_book_carries_id_title_and_author(fresh_client: FlaskClient) -> None:\n    book_id = _add(fresh_client, \"Dune\")\n\n    listed = fresh_client.get(\"/books\").get_json()\n\n    assert {\"id\": book_id, \"title\": \"Dune\", \"author\": \"A\"} in listed\n\n\ndef test_order_survives_reopening_the_store(fresh_client: FlaskClient, store_path: Path) -> None:\n    created = [_add(fresh_client, f\"Book {n}\") for n in range(3)]\n\n    reopened = create_app(Config(database_dsn=str(store_path))).test_client()\n    listed_ids = [book[\"id\"] for book in reopened.get(\"/books\").get_json()]\n\n    assert listed_ids == {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgKbmkxn9xrEVicCMg9Rq","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_019mySEdu7kwPXYya7KYrJab","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/ReadingList/runs/20261023.174350/build/ReadingList/tests/test_remove_book.py","content":"\"\"\"Remove book: DELETE /books/{id} answers 204 for a stored book and 404 for anything else.\"\"\"\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom flask.testing import FlaskClient\n\nfrom app_server import create_app\nfrom app_server.config import Config\n\n\ndef _add(client: FlaskClient, title: str) -> int:\n    return client.post(\"/books\", json={\"title\": title, \"author\": \"A\"}).get_json()[\"id\"]\n\n\ndef _listed_ids(client: FlaskClient) -> list[int]:\n    return [book[\"id\"] for book in client.get(\"/books\").get_json()]\n\n\ndef test_delete_answers_204_with_empty_body(fresh_client: FlaskClient) -> None:\n    book_id = _add(fresh_client, \"Dune\")\n\n    response = fresh_client.delete(f\"/books/{book_id}\")\n\n    assert response.status_code == 204\n    assert response.data == b\"\"\n\n\ndef test_removed_book_is_absent_from_next_list_read(fresh_client: FlaskClient) -> None:\n    book_id = _add(fresh_client, \"Dune\")\n    assert book_id in _listed_ids(fresh_client)\n\n    fresh_client.delete(f\"/books/{book_id}\")\n\n    assert book_id not in _listed_ids(fresh_client)\n\n\ndef test_removed_book_stays_absent_after_reopening_the_store(\n    fresh_client: FlaskClient, store_path: Path\n) -> None:\n    book_id = _add(fresh_client, \"Dune\")\n    fresh_client.delete(f\"/books/{book_id}\")\n\n    reopened = create_app(Config(database_dsn=str(store_path))).test_client()\n\n    assert book_id not in _listed_ids(reopened)\n\n\ndef test_remaining_books_keep_their_order_after_a_middle_removal(fresh_client: FlaskClient) -> None:\n    first, middle, last = (_add(fresh_client, f\"Book {n}\") for n in range(3))\n\n    fresh_client.delete(f\"/books/{middle}\")\n\n    assert _listed_ids(fresh_client) == [first, last]\n\n\ndef test_removing_an_unknown_id_answers_404_with_error_body(fresh_client: FlaskClient) -> None:\n    response = fresh_client.delete(\"/books/999999\")\n\n    assert response.status_code == 404\n    assert isinstance(response.get_json()[\"error\"], str)\n\n\ndef test_removing_the_same_id_twice_answers_404_the_second_time(fresh_client: FlaskClient) -> None:\n    book_id = _add(fresh_client, \"Dune\")\n\n    first = fresh_client.delete(f\"/books/{book_id}\")\n    second = fresh_client.delete(f\"/books/{book_id}\")\n\n    assert first.status_code == 204\n    assert second.status_code == 404\n\n\ndef test_unknown_removal_leaves_the_list_unchanged(fresh_client: FlaskClient) -> None:\n    created = [_add(fresh_client, f\"Book {n}\") for n in range(2)]\n\n assert second.status_code == 404\n\n\ndef test_unknown_removal_leaves_the_list_unchanged(fresh_client: FlaskClient) -> None:\n    created = [_add(fresh_client, f\"Book {n}\") for n in range(2)]\n\n The service imports no Flask. `add_book` validates before any store call and stores the title and author exactly as supplied. `remove_book` calls `books.get` first and returns False without changing anything for an unknown id.\n- **Routes** (`app_server/routes/books.py`, registered in `create_app`): `POST /books` returns 201 with `{id, title, author}`, or 400 with `{\"error\": ...}`. `GET /books` returns the array in id order, with `[]` when empty. `DELETE /books/<int:book_id>` returns 204 with an empty body, or 404 with an error body. A non-integer id does not match the route.\n- **Validation**: a missing, non-string, or whitespace-only title or author raises `ValueError` naming the field. Both fields are named when both are blank. A non-JSON body is treated as an empty submission and gets 400.\n- **Tests**: 50 new tests, using a per-test temporary store with the generated schema applied. The configured `data/app.db` is never written by the tests. The HTTP tests cover the empty list, the response fields, read-back, order across reopening the store, removal persisting across reopening, and repeat or unknown removal.\n- **Existing test changed**: `test_factory_registers_only_the_health_route` is now `test_factory_registers_only_the_declared_routes`, and it expects `/health`, `/books`, and `/books/<int:book_id>`. The old assertion would fail by design once the book routes are registered.\n- **Shared fixtures**: `conftest.py` gained `store_path`, `fresh_app`, `fresh_client`, and `fresh_db`.\n\nResults:\n- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`: 75 passed, 0 failed (baseline was 25 before this block).\n- The 15 declared acceptance criteria from FEATURE-AddBook, ListBooks, RemoveBook, and RejectEmptyFields: 15 passed. I ran them manually from the spec text with the project root on the path. They clean up their own records, and the configured store was left with 0 books.\n\nChoices I made that you may want to change:\n- Validation error wording: a single blank field gives \"title must be non-empty text\", and both give \"title and author must be non-empty text\".\n- The 404 body for an unknown id is `{\"error\": \"no book with id N\"}`.\n- `bin/test.sh` is not built here.
